system.summary: Consonants written plain; vowels as odd digits a e i o u = 1 3 5 7 9 (u also v); even digits 2 4 6 8 (and 0) and the plain letters a e i o u w x y are nulls (Vlnas 2017, table 3).
system.sibling_key: Vlnas 2017 table 3, recovered by Vlnas from inv. 24873 (same microfilm run; 24874 likely the same writer by hand and content); used unchanged.
system.notes: distinct_symbols: tokens in the two transcriptions (digits 0-9, consonant letters, the class tokens S and G, R apart from r, and the plain null letters). nulls.count: null signs that occur (2 4 6 8 0 a e u w). On these photographs the digit 5 and the letter s, and the digit 9 and the letters g and q, have the same shape: the transcription writes class tokens S and G, and the reading chooses by sense (77 such choices in the read words of 24874, 29 in 24876). In this hand 6 is also close to b and t (two repairs in 24874). key_order: the odd digits run in vowel order.

prior_solution.where: No reading of inv. 24874 or 24876 found: Vlnas 2017 (appendix B21, B22: not deciphered, no text printed), the catalogue vetting of 6 Nov 2026 (DECODE dumps, Lasry's list, Tomokiyo, HistoCrypt 2018) and a web search. Vlnas 2017 ch. 4.2 deciphers the neighbouring inv. 24873 and prints the key used here.

solution.what: Frames 24873, 24873_1, 24873_2, 24874 and 24876 taken from the appendix zip of Vlnas 2017 (theses.cz/id/p3p2kb); the thesis read for the key (table 3) and for what it prints.
Vlnas 2017, the catalogue vetting record (DECODE dumps, Lasry, Tomokiyo, HistoCrypt 2018) and one web search: no edition or decipherment of 24874 or 24876 found.
Sign conventions written before any value was applied (class tokens S for s/5 and G for g/q/9); each letter transcribed twice from different crops and reconciled on the image.

Vlnas's table 3 (from inv. 24873) frozen in key_frozen.tsv with our additions (0 null, f long s, class tokens) and applied unchanged to 24874 and 24876; even digits and plain vowel letters behave as nulls throughout.

Frozen key applied to an excerpt of the 24873_2 postscript, which Vlnas did not print: the 14 groups chosen by the solver all give Italian (desidera Sua Altezza ... ragguaglio ... che venendo). Weak: selected and self-scored, no external decipherment to grade against, the freeze rests on file times.
Both letters decrypted with key.tsv and read with every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py fails on any unmarked departure. English translations made.

Independent check (VERIFY.md): blind copy of 11 lines (357 signs) of the two letters and 2 held-out lines before the solver's files were opened; about 7 solver errors and 15 unresolved signs; key confirmed; the verifier's "read in part" was lowered to "decoded, not read" at reading review (6 Nov 2026). Found three places in 24874 where the transcription had followed the sense against the passes, and asked for strict counts and an honest account of the held-out excerpt.

After the check: 24874 L09 and L12 written as the passes saw them (6, l; a blotted sign as [?]); three missed or misread null signs added in 24876. politico and avertimenti are now marked repairs; 24874 verbatim fell from 78 to 76 of 116.

Reading review, independent of the solver: each cipher sentence read against the translation and three lines per letter against the photograph. 24874: 2 of 6 cipher sentences read, the others have holes or guesses (sentence check in Italian: 1 of 8 clean). 24876: 1 of 3 reads, with holes at its head (0 of 2 scored clean). Holes in most sentences, so both letters were lowered from "read in part" to "decoded, not read" and the target to "not read".

texts.label: inv. 24874 (Vlnas 2017 appendix B21)
texts.summary: An outline only (the letter is decoded, not read). The writer, reporting for someone he calls 'l'arciduca mio signore', says that 'Sua [...]' (the title is a hole) took great consolation from Piccolomini's [?letter] and wishes 'una giusta et per [...] relatione', since Piccolomini knows best which advices are needed; the middle mentions a 'modo et governo' and 'the political government'. The clear tail announces the coming of Don Miguel de Salamanca. Archduke Leopold Wilhelm was named governor of the Spanish Netherlands at the end of 1646, which fits, but the text does not name him.
texts.note: Reviewed 6 Nov 2026 against the translation and the photograph, independently of the solver. The cipher part has six sentences, and only two read: 'Desidera dunque una giusta et per [...] relatione, mentre lei sa meglio queli avertimenti [?che siano] necessarii' (one hole, one guess) and 'Di quelo so tralascio per non tediarla.' The middle (L03-L09: 'gran consolazione dalla di lei [?lettera] ... si esibisce di darli parte minutamente ... dal governo politico') gives an outline, but its two sentences carry 7 and 6 holes or guesses each. The opening has 11 holes or guesses in its 22 words (L01-L03). The close does not build a sentence either: L14-L20 have 10 holes in 33 words, and there is a hole in every clause. With language 'it', the sentence check finds 1 of 8 cipher sentences clean, and 15% on the file. Of the 76 words decoded verbatim, 43 rest on an s/5 or g/q/9 choice made by sense. Three sampled lines (L03-L05) match the photograph as far as letters 15-20 px high allow. Most sentences have holes, so the letter is decoded, not read. A further pass on L01-L03 and L14-L20, ideally from a clean scan, may change that. Words 116: 76 decoded verbatim from the signs (65.5%), of which 33 with no s/i or g/q/u/v class choice; 6 with a marked repair; 7 guessed from context; 27 holes. 'dal' (L09) rests on a doubtful sign.

texts.label: inv. 24876 (Vlnas 2017 appendix B22)
texts.summary: Two cipher passages between clear news (the letter is decoded, not read). Block A is fragments: Bavaria, 'so that we must fight', complaints already answered. Block B, with holes at its head: 'the Duke of Bavaria wants peace by all means, so that he [?can] consider the advantage we shall have'. The clear text reports prisoners' news of the enemy and, from Vienna, a journey to Linz and then Ratisbona. Fits Bavaria's moves toward a separate truce in late 1646 (Ulm, March 1647); context only.
texts.note: Reviewed 6 Nov 2026 against the translation and the photograph, independently of the solver. The cipher has 50 words in three sentences, and every sentence has holes. Block B holds after three opening holes and one guess: '[...] [...] [...] duca di Baviera vuoglia in tutti modi la pace, sì che [?puol] considerare l'avantaggio che noi havremo.' Block A does not build sentences. 'di Baviera non [?vengono] [...] [...] lo che si dobiamo battere [...] [...] [...] di lamentationi' has 6 holes or guesses in 17 words. 'tutta già se li risponde [...] [...] [...] et il dovere [...]' has 4 in 12. With language 'it', the sentence check finds no clean cipher sentence. Its clean sentences on the file (28%) are all in the clear passages, which are draft readings and are not counted. It also skips the second sentence of block A as too fragmentary to score. Of the 32 words decoded verbatim, 18 rest on an s/5 or g/q/9 choice made by sense. The sampled lines of both blocks match the photograph as far as letters 15-20 px high allow. Only one of three sentences reads, so the letter is decoded, not read, until block A reads. Words 50: 32 decoded verbatim from the signs (64.0%), of which 14 with no class choice; 4 with a marked repair; 2 guessed; 12 holes. Another hand than 24874, same key.
